Last year in April, my partner visited Alexandra Surgery due to a health concern. The doctor ran several tests, including a blood test that revealed low vitamin D levels. However, no one at the surgery communicated this important result to him. Although someone apparently prescribed vitamin D 2000, he was never informed about the prescription or told to collect it.

A full year passed without any treatment or follow-up, during which his symptoms worsened. Only recently, after further health issues and new tests, was the deficiency addressed — now requiring a double dose of vitamin D.

This shows a clear lack of communication and negligence from the staff involved. Failing to inform a patient about test results and prescriptions is not just careless; it puts their health at risk.
